title: The truce with Qashtāla runs out, Gharnāṭa holds a just cause, and the amir declares war for the realm's independence and marches north
source: Trent's account; the casus belli from the save of 20 May 1363

title: At the outbreak: the Marīnids hold 58 Castilian towns as far as Toledo, and Qashtāla has 183 men in its pool; Portugal 3,700. Gharnāṭa has 1,900 of 6,400 and only 57 in the treasury. Sovereignty 100, influence −12.2
The court's first aim in the war: to knock Portugal out, as it had already made its own peace with the Marīnids
The gain of the Marīnid war: the court kept the ṭāʾifas of Balansiyya and Mursiyya out of it, and they come to the war of independence untouched
Baena becomes the first town of the reconquered valley whose people count themselves Andalusī again. They are still Christian
source: save of 20 May 1363 (the change falls between the saves of 26 June 1360 and 20 May 1363)

title: Arghūn joins the war against Gharnāṭa on Qashtāla's side, though only months before it had been Qashtāla's enemy
source: Trent's account; by the save of 20 May 1363 Aragon was already fighting beside Castile against Morocco

title: Al-Ḥājj Yūsuf I dies at Ayamonte on the march into Portugal, ten weeks into the war for the realm's independence, aged forty-five, after thirty years on the throne
source: save of 2 August 1363 (death dated 1 August); Trent's account

title: Saʿd ibn Yūsuf, fifteen, succeeds his father. Naṣr al-Istijjī of the house of Istijja is made regent until the young sultan comes of age on 18 January 1364
The regent Naṣr al-Istijjī marries Duʿāʾ, the late amir's Marīnid widow and minister, within days of Yūsuf's death
source: save of 2 August 1363 (already married); Trent's account

title: The treasury holds 24 against expenses of 89 a month and an income of 52
